title: Predictive Surge Corridors & Throttle-Aware Autoscale — Q2 Roadmap
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Purpose: Define and deliver a quarterly roadmap for predictive surge corridors and throttle-aware autoscaling for Dedicated capacity. The initiative targets reducing hard-failure customer incidents during unusual traffic spikes, lowering median cost/unit during transient surges by enabling predictive preheat corridors, and adding throttle-aware routing as a graceful degradation mechanism. Scope: 1) Predictive Surge Corridors: experiment and ship model that identifies temporal surge windows per customer pool and auto-provisions short-lived warm capacity ahead of demand. 2) Throttle-Aware Autoscale: add server-side policy controls and router signals to reduce low-priority work during constrained capacity while preserving higher priority SLAs. 3) Cost Guardrails: integrate cost signal into autoscale decisions (max spend per-minute budget and rollback trigger). Out of scope: new billing model changes and on-prem private console features for this quarter.
acceptance_criteria: Predictive surge classifier deployed to canary pool and observing >60% true positives on historical test set
Autoscale policy exposes throttle-aware priority levels and is enforced in Dedicated router (canary) without SLA regressions for P0 customers
Cost guardrail hook triggers scale-down / fallback in at least two simulated surge scenarios and emits audit events to Console
Runbook and playbooks published and reviewed by SRE and Support; two rehearsals completed
Metrics and dashboards available: surge-detection-rate, canary-latency-penalty, incremental-cost-per-surge, and customer-error-rate
milestones: 2026-04-01: Data collection pipeline and feature proto in ENG lab
2026-04-20: Initial surge classifier and local validation
2026-05-05: Canary deploy of throttle-aware policy for 5% of traffic
2026-06-24: Broad rollout to Dedicated regional pools
kpis: Reduce hard-failure incidents during surges by 70% for targeted pools
Decrease median extra-cost-per-surge by 30% compared to baseline
Maintain 99.9% P0 latency SLO during canary windows
Number of customers using predictive corridor opt-in > 10 by end of quarter
risks: Surge classifier false positives increase cost without improving availability
Throttle policies may introduce unexpected latency regressions for mid-priority workloads
Insufficient telemetry to attribute cost changes to corridor behavior
Cross-region capacity constraints complicate predictive warmups leading to cascading fallbacks
decisions_needed: Risk budget allocation for false positive induced preheats (finance & product)
Default priority mapping for throttle-aware policies (PM + SRE + Eng consensus required)
Opt-in versus opt-out default for existing Dedicated customers
